en: Majjhima Nikāya 4:
Bhayabherava Sutta.
Thus have I heard—
On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.
Then the brahmin Jāṇussoṇi approached the Blessed One and exchanged greetings with him.
When they had concluded their courteous and amiable conversation, he sat down to one side. Seated to one side, the brahmin Jāṇussoṇi said this to the Blessed One:
“Master Gotama, those clansmen who have gone forth from the home life into homelessness out of faith,
inspired by Master Gotama— they have Master Gotama as their leader, Master Gotama is their benefactor,
and Master Gotama is their inspirer; moreover, that people follows Master Gotama’s example.”
“So it is, brahmin; so it is, brahmin.
Those clansmen, brahmin, who have gone forth from the home life into homelessness out of faith, inspired by me—they have me as their forerunner, they have me as their benefactor, I am their inspirer;
and that generation follows my example.”
“Indeed, Master Gotama, remote forest and wilderness dwellings are difficult to approach; solitude is hard to practice, and it is difficult to find delight in being alone.
The forests seem to drag away the mind of a bhikkhu who has not attained concentration.
“It is so, brahmin, it is so! It is exactly as you say.”
"Indeed, Brahmin, remote forest lodgings in the wilderness and jungle-thickets are difficult to approach; seclusion is hard to practice, and solitude is hard to enjoy.
The forests, it seems, carry away the mind of a bhikkhu who has not attained concentration.
It occurred to me too, Brahmin, before my enlightenment, while I was still an unenlightened bodhisatta: [that these things were so]."
“‘Indeed, remote forest and jungle dwellings are difficult to approach; seclusion is hard to practice, and solitude is hard to enjoy;
the woods, it seems, carry away the mind of a bhikkhu who has not attained concentration.
This, brahmin, occurred to me.”
‘Whatever recluses or brahmins, with their bodily actions unpurified, resort to remote lodgings in forest groves and jungle thickets—
it is because of the fault of their unpurified bodily actions that those venerable recluses and brahmins summon upon themselves unwholesome fear and terror.’
"Moreover, it is not because my bodily action is impure that I resort to remote lodgings in the wilderness and forests;
rather, my bodily action is pure.
For I am one of those noble ones who, with pure bodily action, resort to remote lodgings in the wilderness and forests."
"Seeing this purity of bodily action within myself, brahmin, I became even more confident about dwelling in the forest.
Then, brahmin, it occurred to me:
'Whatever ascetics or brahmins have impure verbal conduct...'"
Those whose mental actions are impure...

[and so on] ...those who live an impure livelihood resort to remote lodgings in forest thickets and jungle groves. It is indeed because of the corruption of their impure livelihood that those venerable recluses and brahmins invite upon themselves unwholesome fear and terror.
But I do not live an impure livelihood when I resort to remote lodgings in forest thickets and jungle groves.
"I am one of pure livelihood.
For I am one among those noble ones of pure livelihood who resort to remote lodgings in forest thickets and jungle retreats.
Seeing this purity of livelihood in myself, O Brahmin, I became even more confident in dwelling in the forest.
Then, brahmin, this occurred to me: ‘Whatever ascetics or brahmins,

being covetous and having intense lust for sensual pleasures, resort to remote lodgings in forest groves and jungle thickets— surely those venerable ones, because of that defect of covetousness and intense lust for sensual pleasures, [will fall away].’”
Some ascetics and brahmins proclaim unwholesome things as fearful and terrifying.
However, I do not dwell in remote lodgings in forest groves and wilderness areas while being covetous and possessed by intense lust for sensual pleasures;
rather, I am free from covetousness.
‘Those noble ones who, free from covetousness, resort to remote lodgings in the wilderness and forests—I am one of them.
Seeing this lack of covetousness in myself, brahmin, I gained even greater confidence in dwelling in the wilderness.
Then, brahmin, this occurred to me:
‘Whatever ascetics or brahmins, with minds full of ill will and corrupt intentions,
resort to remote lodgings in forest thickets and jungle retreats,
it is because of the taint of those ill-willed and corruptly intended minds that these worthy ascetics and brahmins invite upon themselves unwholesome fear and terror.’
"Yet it is not with a mind of ill will or a corrupt intention that I resort to remote lodgings in forest thickets and jungle groves;
I am one whose mind is imbued with loving-kindness.
For I am one of those noble ones who, with minds imbued with loving-kindness, resort to remote lodgings in forest thickets and jungle groves."
"Seeing this state of loving-kindness within myself, brahmin, I became even more confident about dwelling in the forest.
Then, brahmin, it occurred to me:
'Whatever ascetics or brahmins are obsessed by sloth and torpor while staying in remote forest and jungle retreats...'"
Those venerable recluses and brahmins resort to remote lodgings in forests and jungle-thickets because they are defiled by the obsession with sloth and torpor;
it is for this reason that those venerable ones invite upon themselves unwholesome fear and terror.
However, I do not resort to remote lodgings in forests and jungle-thickets while obsessed by sloth and torpor.
“I am free from sloth and torpor.
Indeed, I am one of those noble ones who, being free from sloth and torpor, resort to remote lodgings in forest thickets and wilderness areas.
Seeing this freedom from sloth and torpor within myself, O brahmin, I gained even greater confidence in dwelling in the forest.
Then, brahmin, this occurred to me:
‘Whatever ascetics or brahmins, agitated and with unpeaceful minds, resort to remote lodgings in forest thickets and jungle retreats,
it is surely because of the defect of their agitated and unpeaceful minds that those worthy ascetics and brahmins [do so].’
They call the unwholesome fear and terror.
Yet it is not with an agitated and unpacified mind that I resort to remote lodgings in forest thickets and wilderness areas;
I am one whose mind is pacified.
‘For I am one of those noble ones whose minds are tranquil and who resort to remote lodgings in forest thickets and jungle retreats.
Seeing this tranquility of mind within myself, brahmin, I became even more confident in dwelling in the forest.
Then, brahmin, this occurred to me:
‘Whatever ascetics or brahmins, being doubtful and wavering, resort to remote lodgings in forest thickets and jungle retreats,
it is because of the defect of doubt and wavering that those venerable ascetics and brahmins summon unwholesome fear and terror.
But I do not resort to remote lodgings in forest thickets and jungle retreats while being doubtful and wavering.’
"I have crossed over doubt.
For I am one among those noble ones who, having crossed over doubt, resort to remote lodgings in forest thickets and jungle retreats.
Seeing this state of having crossed over doubt within myself, O brahmin, I became even more confident in dwelling in the forest.
Then, brahmin, this occurred to me:
‘Whatever ascetics or brahmins, praising themselves and disparaging others, resort to remote lodgings in forest thickets and wilderness areas—
it is surely because of the fault of self-praise and disparagement of others that those worthy ascetics and brahmins [suffer].’
They call the unwholesome "fear and terror.
Yet it is not because I am one who praises myself and disparages others that I resort to remote lodgings in forest thickets and wilderness areas;
rather, it is because I am one who does not praise myself and does not disparage others.
‘Those noble ones who do not praise themselves and do not disparage others, who resort to remote lodgings in the wilderness and forests—I am one among them.
Seeing this lack of self-praise and lack of disparagement of others within myself, O brahmin, I became even more confident in dwelling in the wilderness.
Then, brahmin, this occurred to me:
‘Whatever ascetics or brahmins, being timid and of a fearful nature, resort to remote lodgings in forest thickets and jungle retreats—
it is because of the fault of their timidity and fearfulness that those venerable ascetics and brahmins invite upon themselves unwholesome fear and terror.’
"Yet it is not because I am timid or of a fearful nature that I resort to remote lodgings in forest thickets and wilderness areas;
I am one who has no horripilation. Indeed, I am one of those noble ones who, free from horripilation, resort to remote lodgings in forest thickets and wilderness areas."
"Seeing this freedom from horripilation within myself, O brahmin, I became even more confident regarding dwelling in the forest.
Then, brahmin, it occurred to me:
'Whatever ascetics or brahmins, desiring gain, honor, and fame, [go] to the remote forests and woods...'"
Those venerable recluses and brahmins resort to remote lodgings in the forest and jungle groves because of the corruption of desiring gain, honor, and fame;
it is for that reason that they invite upon themselves unwholesome fear and terror.
But I do not resort to remote lodgings in the forest and jungle groves out of a desire for gain, honor, and fame.
"I am one of few desires. Indeed, I am one among those noble ones of few desires who resort to remote lodgings in forest thickets and wilderness areas.
Seeing this quality of fewness of desires within myself, O brahmin, I became even more confident in dwelling in the forest.
Then, brahmin, it occurred to me:
‘Whatever ascetics or brahmins, being lazy and of inferior energy, resort to remote lodgings in forest thickets and jungle retreats—
it is because of the fault of their laziness and inferior energy that these worthy ascetics and brahmins invite upon themselves unwholesome fear and terror.’
"Yet it is not because I am lazy or of inferior energy that I resort to remote lodgings in forest groves and wilderness areas;
rather, I am one who has aroused energy. Indeed, I am one among those noble ones who, having aroused energy, resort to remote lodgings in forest groves and wilderness areas."
"Seeing this arousal of energy within myself, brahmin, I became even more confident about dwelling in the forest.
Then, brahmin, it occurred to me:
'Whatever ascetics or brahmins are muddle-minded and lacking clear comprehension while staying in remote forest lodgings in the woods..."
Those venerable recluses and brahmins resort to remote lodgings in forests and jungle thickets because of the fault of being muddled in mindfulness and lacking clear comprehension;
it is for this reason that those worthy ones invite upon themselves unwholesome fear and terror.
However, I do not resort to remote lodgings in forests and jungle thickets while being muddled in mindfulness and lacking clear comprehension.
“I am one whose mindfulness is established.
For I am one of those noble ones who, with mindfulness established, resort to remote lodgings in forest thickets and jungle retreats.
It was by seeing this quality of established mindfulness within myself, brahmin, that I became even more confident about dwelling in the forest.
Then, brahmin, this occurred to me:
‘Whatever ascetics or brahmins, being unconcentrated and with wandering minds, resort to remote lodgings in forest thickets and jungle retreats—
it is surely because of the defect of being unconcentrated and having wandering minds that those worthy ascetics and brahmins [do so].’
They call unwholesome states fear and terror.
Yet I do not frequent remote lodgings in forest thickets and wilderness areas while being unconcentrated and of distracted mind;
I am one who possesses concentration.
‘For those noble ones who are perfected in concentration and resort to remote lodgings in forest thickets and jungle retreats—I am one among them.
Seeing this perfection of concentration within myself, brahmin, I became even more confident in dwelling in the forest.
Then, brahmin, this thought occurred to me:
‘Whatever recluses or brahmins, being of poor wisdom and dull-witted, resort to remote lodgings in forest thickets and jungle retreats—
it is because of the fault of their poor wisdom and dull-wittedness that those venerable recluses and brahmins summon upon themselves unwholesome fear and terror.
But I do not resort to remote lodgings in forest thickets and jungle retreats while being of poor wisdom and dull-witted.’
“I am one who is endowed with wisdom.
For I am one among those noble ones endowed with wisdom who resort to remote lodgings in forest groves and jungle thickets.
Seeing this perfection of wisdom within myself, brahmin, I became even more confident about dwelling in the forest.
The sixteenfold exposition is finished.
Then, brahmin, this occurred to me:
"What if I were to [observe] those nights that are well-known and well-recognized?"

‘On the fourteenth, the fifteenth, and the eighth day of the lunar fortnight—on such nights as these, I shall dwell in such dwelling places as are terrifying and hair-raising, such as grove-shrines, forest-shrines, and tree-shrines; perhaps I might behold fear and dread.
Then, Brahmin, after some time, there came those nights which were well-known and well-observed...
On the fourteenth, the fifteenth, and the eighth day of the fortnight— on such nights as these,
I dwell in such dwellings as are haunted by forest shrines, grove shrines, or tree shrines, which are terrifying and hair-raising. And while I am dwelling there,
O brahmin, either a deer comes by, or a peacock drops a branch, or the wind stirs a cluster of leaves.
Then, brahmin, this occurred to me:
‘Surely that fear and terror are coming.
Then, brahmin, this occurred to me:
‘Why indeed do I dwell merely anticipating fear?
Suppose that, whenever such fear and terror come upon me as they truly are, I were to overcome that fear and terror by being exactly as I am?
While I was walking back and forth, Brahmin, that fear and terror came upon me.
So, brahmin, I neither stood, nor sat, nor lay down until, while walking back and forth, I had dispelled that fear and dread. Brahmin,
when that fear and dread came upon me while I was standing,
I neither walked, nor sat, nor lay down until, while standing, I had dispelled that fear and dread.
“Brahmin, while I am sitting, that fear and terror come upon me.
Then, brahmin, I neither lie down, nor stand, nor walk about, until while still sitting I have dispelled that fear and terror.
Brahmin, while I am lying down, that fear and terror come upon me.”
Thus, brahmin, I neither sat down, nor stood, nor walked about, until while lying down I had dispelled that fear and dread.
Furthermore, brahmin, there are some ascetics and brahmins who perceive night as day, and they perceive day as night.
I say of those ascetics and brahmins that they dwell in confusion.
"But as for me, brahmin, when it is night I perceive it as night, and when it is day I perceive it as day.
And if anyone, brahmin, speaking rightly were to say:

'A being subject to non-delusion has appeared in the world for the welfare of many, for the happiness of many, out of compassion for the world, for the good, welfare, and happiness of gods and humans,' it is of me that one speaking rightly would say this."
‘A being not subject to delusion has arisen in the world for the welfare of many, for the happiness of many, out of compassion for the world, for the good, welfare, and happiness of gods and humans.
And, brahmin, my energy was aroused and unflagging, my mindfulness was established and unconfused, my body was tranquil and unstrained, and my mind was concentrated and one-pointed.

Thus, brahmin, secluded from sensual pleasures, secluded from unwholesome states, I entered and dwelt in the first jhāna, which is accompanied by applied and sustained thought, with rapture and happiness born of seclusion.

With the stilling of applied and sustained thought, I entered and dwelt in the second jhāna, which has internal confidence and mental unification, is without applied and sustained thought, and possesses rapture and happiness born of concentration.
And with the fading away of rapture, I dwelt equanimous, mindful, and clearly comprehending, experiencing happiness with the body; I entered and dwelt in the third jhāna.
I entered and dwelt in the third jhāna, which the Noble Ones describe as: “Equanimous, mindful, and dwelling in happiness.

With the abandoning of pleasure and the abandoning of pain, and with the previous disappearance of joy and grief, I entered and dwelt in the fourth jhāna, which is neither-painful-nor-pleasant and possesses purity of mindfulness through equanimity.
When my mind was thus concentrated, purified, bright, unblemished, rid of imperfection, malleable, and wieldy...
When my mind was thus settled and unshakable, I directed it toward the knowledge of recollecting past lives.
I recollected my manifold past lives, that is to say:
one birth, two births, three births, four births, five births...
“...ten births, twenty births, thirty births, forty births, fifty births, a hundred births, a thousand births, a hundred thousand births;
many aeons of world-contraction, many aeons of world-expansion, many aeons of both world-contraction and expansion:
‘There I was, with such a name, such a clan, such an appearance, such food, such experience of pleasure and pain.’”

"Thus was the limit of my lifespan; passing away from there, I arose in another state. There too I had such a name, such a clan, such an appearance, such food, such experiences of pleasure and pain, and such a limit to my lifespan. Passing away from there, I reappeared here.
In this way, I recollect my manifold past lives with their modes and details.
This, brahmin, was the first true knowledge attained by me in the first watch of the night:
ignorance was destroyed and true knowledge arose; darkness was dispelled and light arose, as happens for one who dwells diligent, ardent, and resolute.

With my mind thus concentrated, pure, bright, unblemished, rid of defilement, malleable, workable, steady, and attained to imperturbability, I directed my mind toward the knowledge of the passing away and rebirth of beings.
Thus, with the divine eye, purified and surpassing that of humans, I see beings passing away and being reborn—
lowly and exalted, beautiful and ugly, fortunate and unfortunate— and I understand how beings fare according to their kamma:
"Alas, these worthy beings were possessed of misconduct of body, possessed of misconduct of speech, and possessed of misconduct of mind..."
They were possessed of these qualities: they were revilers of the noble ones, held wrong views, and undertook actions based on wrong views;
with the breakup of the body, after death, they were reborn in a state of deprivation, a bad destination, a lower realm, even in hell.
But these venerable beings were possessed of good conduct of body, possessed of good conduct of speech, and possessed of good conduct of mind.
‘They do not revile the noble ones, they hold right view, and they undertake actions based on right view;

with the breakup of the body, after death, they have reappeared in a happy destination, a heavenly world. Thus, with the divine eye, purified and surpassing that of humans, I see beings passing away and being reborn—low and high, beautiful and ugly, fortunate and unfortunate—and I understand how beings fare according to their kamma.
“This, brahmin, was the second true knowledge attained by me in the middle watch of the night;
ignorance was destroyed and true knowledge arose, darkness was dispelled and light arose, as happens for one who dwells diligent, ardent, and resolute.
With my mind thus concentrated, purified, cleansed, stainless, free from defilements, supple, wieldy, stable, and imperturbable, I directed it toward the knowledge of the destruction of the taints.”
Thus I directly knew, as it really is: "This is suffering"; I directly knew, as it really is:
"This is the origin of suffering"; I directly knew, as it really is: "This is the cessation of suffering"; I directly knew, as it really is: "This is the way leading to the cessation of suffering."
‘These are the taints,’ I directly knew as it really is; ‘this is the origin of the taints,’ I directly knew as it really is;
‘this is the cessation of the taints,’ I directly knew as it really is; ‘this is the way leading to the cessation of the taints,’ I directly knew as it really is.
As I knew thus and saw thus, my mind was liberated from the taint of sensual desire, my mind was liberated from the taint of existence, and my mind was liberated from the taint of ignorance.
When it was liberated, there came the knowledge: "It is liberated.
I directly realized: "Birth is exhausted, the holy life has been lived, what had to be done has been done, there is no more of this state of being."
"Indeed, brahmin, this third true knowledge was attained by me in the last watch of the night;
ignorance was destroyed and true knowledge arose, darkness was dispelled and light arose, as happens for one who dwells diligent, ardent, and resolute.
Now, brahmin, it may be that you think thus:"
‘Even now, surely the ascetic Gotama is not free from lust, not free from hatred, and not free from delusion; that is why he resorts to remote lodgings in the wilderness and forests.
But, brahmin, this should not be viewed in such a way.
Brahmin, seeing two purposes, I resort to remote lodgings in the wilderness and forests.
“Out of regard for his own dwelling in happiness in this very life, and out of compassion for future generations.
“Truly, Master Gotama has shown great compassion for future generations, as befits one who is an Arahant, a perfectly awakened Buddha.
Excellent, Master Gotama! Excellent, Master Gotama!”
"Just as, Master Gotama, one might set upright what had been overturned, or reveal what was hidden,
or show the way to one who was lost, or bring an oil lamp into the darkness so that those with eyes might see forms—
just so has the Dhamma been elucidated by Master Gotama in many ways."
“I go for refuge to Master Gotama, and to the Dhamma, and to the Saṅgha of bhikkhus.
May Master Gotama accept me as a lay follower who has gone for refuge from this day forth for as long as life lasts.
The *Bhayabherava Sutta*, the fourth, is finished.
